items.title: Spline-expanded logistic regression on curated descriptors
items.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member that is a logistic regression on the 10 curated descriptors. Build the features with sklearn SplineTransformer (n_knots=5, degree=3, extrapolation='constant') fitted on the training fold only, followed by StandardScaler. Fit LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed). Its test probabilities go into the same rank average as the three XGBoost members, weighted equally. This gives a smooth, additive, GAM-like physchem model that the tree ensemble cannot express.

items.title: RBF SVC on quantile-scaled curated descriptors
items.spec: Add a rank-averaged member that is a probability-free SVM: QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=200, output_distribution='normal') then StandardScaler on the 10 curated descriptors, fitted on the training fold only. Use SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1.0, gamma='scale') and take decision_function on the test fold as the score, which is rank-averaged with the other members, so no Platt scaling is needed. Keep the three XGBoost members unchanged.

items.title: Rule-of-five and ring-count descriptor extension
items.spec: Extend featurize() with about six extra columns that are cheap and BBB-relevant: number of aromatic rings (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAromaticRings), number of aliphatic rings, heavy-atom count, number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (MW>500, cLogP>5, HBD>5, HBA>10), halogen count, and amide count from the SMARTS C(=O)N. Keep the existing 10 columns. Feed this 16-column matrix to the existing descriptor-based member only; the three fingerprint XGBoost members stay as they are.

items.title: Per-node column subsampling in the XGBoost members
items.spec: In each of the three XGBoost fits, replace colsample_bytree=0.3 with colsample_bytree=1.0 and colsample_bynode=0.3. Keep every other setting, the seed, and the rank averaging. This changes how feature sampling is applied, from once per tree to once per split, so trees see more varied candidate features within a single tree.

items.title: Coarse histogram binning as a regularizer on the descriptor member
items.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged XGBoost member trained on the 10 curated descriptors only, with tree_method='hist', max_bin=16, max_depth=4, n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, min_child_weight=5, random_state=seed. Coarse split thresholds act as a smoothing prior on the continuous physchem features. Give this member the same weight as each of the others in the rank average.

items.title: Logit averaging instead of rank averaging across members
items.spec: Replace the final rankdata-based combination with an average of logits. For each member, convert its test probabilities p to log(p/(1-p)) after clipping to [1e-6, 1-1e-6]. Average the logits across members with equal weights, then map the mean back through a sigmoid to get the returned probability of class 1. The output stays in [0,1] and keeps the same ordering semantics, but it preserves the magnitude of confident predictions rather than discarding it.

items.title: Chirality-aware Morgan fingerprint
items.spec: In fingerprints(), build the Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, includeChirality=True) instead of the current default, and keep the count-free presence bits. Stereo-specific environments then become distinct bits. Leave the atom-pair and MACCS sets unchanged, and keep the three-member XGBoost ensemble structure as it is.

items.title: Quantile-scaled k-nearest-neighbour member on curated descriptors
items.spec: Add a rank-averaged member that is a KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=25, weights='distance') on the 10 curated descriptors. Scale them with QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on the training fold, then apply StandardScaler. Use the predicted probability of class 1 as the member score. The purpose is a local, non-parametric physchem view that differs from both the trees and the linear models.

items.title: Gasteiger partial-charge histogram features
items.spec: Extend the feature set with a 12-bin histogram of per-atom Gasteiger partial charges. Compute them with AllChem-free rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(m) on each molecule, take the charge values of heavy atoms, clip them to [-0.5, 0.5], and count them into 12 equal-width bins. Also add the total positive and total negative charge sums. Use the result as an extra fourth member, an XGBoost trained on these 14 columns plus the 10 curated descriptors, rank-averaged with the existing members.

items.title: Class-balanced scale_pos_weight in every XGBoost member
items.spec: Set scale_pos_weight to the ratio of negative to positive training labels, computed inside fit_predict from train_y, in each of the three XGBoost fits. Everything else stays the same, including the seed, the feature sets, and the rank averaging. This reweights the minority class in the gradient and may shift the tree splits toward better separation of the rarer class, which AUROC rewards. It was not tried for the boosting members, only for random forest.

items.title: Add ExtraTrees member to ensemble (replicate)
items.spec: In fit_predict, add a fourth rank-averaged member: sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) trained on the horizontally concatenated Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS matrices. Rank-average it with the three XGBoost members with equal weight, then min-max normalise as before.

items.title: ExtraTrees plus random-subspace XGBoost combined
items.spec: Keep the three per-feature-set XGBoost members. Add two members: an ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2) on concatenated features, and a random-subspace XGBoost bag of 12 small models (200 rounds, depth 4, colsample_bytree 0.15) on the concatenated features, each with a different seed. Rank-average all five members equally.

items.title: Multi-scale Morgan counts radius 1 and 3
items.spec: Replace the single radius-2 Morgan bit matrix with the horizontal concatenation of 1024-bit count Morgan fingerprints at radius 1 and radius 3 (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Keep the atom-pair and MACCS members and the rank averaging unchanged.

items.title: Topological torsion fingerprint member
items.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost member (same hyperparameters as the others) on 2048-bit topological torsion count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048). Include it in the rank average with equal weight.

items.title: Label smoothing for XGBoost targets
items.spec: Train each XGBoost member as an XGBRegressor with objective reg:logistic on soft targets 0.05 for class 0 and 0.95 for class 1, with otherwise identical hyperparameters. Use predict as the score for rank averaging.

items.title: Input bit-dropout augmentation
items.spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, build an augmented training set by stacking the original rows with one copy where each nonzero feature is zeroed with probability 0.15 (seeded numpy RNG). Duplicate the labels. Predict on the unmodified test features.

items.title: Seed-averaged ensemble bagging
items.spec: Wrap the three-member ensemble so that it is run with 3 different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), using reduced n_estimators=300 per model to stay inside the time limit. Rank-average the member predictions across seeds, then normalise. Reuse the fingerprints computed once.

items.title: DART booster members
items.spec: Change each XGBoost member to booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, n_estimators=400, and the other parameters unchanged. Check that runtime stays within the budget. Keep the rank averaging.

items.title: CNS MPO desirability rank member
items.spec: Compute a parameter-free CNS MPO style score from RDKit values: piecewise-linear desirability for MolLogP (best ≤3), MolWt (best ≤360), TPSA (best 40–90), HBD (best ≤0.5) and the count of basic amines. Sum the desirabilities. Add the rank of this score as a fourth ensemble member with weight 0.5 relative to the weight of 1 for each XGBoost member.

items.title: Rank-averaging weights from inner OOF AUROC
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 3-fold stratified CV on the training set for each of the three XGBoost members, using 150 rounds for speed. Compute the OOF AUROC of each member. Use weights proportional to max(AUROC-0.5, 0)^2 when rank-averaging the final full-fit members.

items.title: Seed-averaged ExtraTrees fourth member
items.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member to the existing three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble: an ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8) trained on the horizontal concatenation of the three existing feature matrices (Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS). To cut variance, fit it three times with random_state = seed, seed+1, seed+2, average the three predict_proba class-1 columns, then rankdata that average and add it to `total` exactly like the other members (so total is the sum of four rank vectors before min-max scaling). Keep everything else unchanged. This both replicates the earlier single-seed ExtraTrees result (0.0866) and reduces its run-to-run noise; it should stay well inside the 10-minute budget.

items.title: ExtraTrees plus random-subspace XGBoost together
items.spec: Combine the two best-performing single additions into one ensemble. Keep the three existing per-feature-set XGBoost members and their rank contributions. Then build the pooled feature matrix X = hstack(Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS) and add two further rank-averaged members: (a) an ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on X, and (b) a random-subspace XGBoost: 24 XGBClassifier models (n_estimators=200, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.08, subsample=0.8, min_child_weight=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed+k), each fit on a random subset of 30% of the columns of X drawn with a numpy Generator seeded from seed; average the 24 class-1 probability vectors before ranking. Final prediction is the min-max scaled sum of the five rank vectors.

items.title: ExtraTrees on each feature set instead of XGBoost
items.spec: Replace the XGBoost member on each of the three feature sets with an ExtraTreesClassifier, keeping the ensemble structure identical. For each of the three feature matrices (Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS) fit ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=1000, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, bootstrap=False, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), take the class-1 probability, rankdata it and sum across the three members, then min-max scale as now. This tests whether the earlier ExtraTrees gain came from the model family rather than from pooling features, and it removes all XGBoost hyperparameters from the script.

items.title: Seed averaging of the three XGBoost members
items.spec: Keep the architecture exactly as it is, but reduce prediction variance by fitting each of the three per-feature-set XGBoost members with three different seeds instead of one. For each feature set, loop over s in (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000), fit XGBClassifier with the current hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, random_state=s) and also pass that same s so the subsample/colsample draws differ, average the three class-1 probability vectors, rankdata the average, and add it to `total`. This is nine fits per fold rather than three; verify the job still finishes under 10 minutes (reduce n_estimators to 400 if needed).

items.title: Inner out-of-fold weights for the rank average
items.spec: Replace the equal-weight rank average with weights learned from the training data. Inside fit_predict, run a single 5-fold StratifiedKFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) over the training set to obtain out-of-fold class-1 probabilities for each of the three feature-set XGBoost members. Compute each member's out-of-fold AUROC a_i, convert to weights w_i = max(a_i - 0.5, 0.01) and normalise them to sum to 1. Then refit each member on the full training set as now and form total = sum_i w_i * rankdata(p_i) before the existing min-max scaling. Keep the hyperparameters and feature sets unchanged; this costs one extra pass of the three models (six fits per fold total), which should fit the time budget.

items.title: Inner-holdout early stopping for the boosting round count
items.spec: Let the data choose the number of boosting rounds for each feature-set member instead of fixing 500. For each of the three feature sets, split the training rows once with StratifiedShuffleSplit (test_size=0.2, random_state=seed), fit XGBClassifier(n_estimators=2000, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, eval_metric='auc', early_stopping_rounds=50, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the 80% with the 20% as eval_set, read best_iteration, then refit a fresh model on all training rows with n_estimators set to int(best_iteration * 1.25) + 1 (clipped to [100, 1500]). Rank-average the three refit models as now. Note early_stopping_rounds must be a constructor argument, not a fit argument, in the installed XGBoost.

items.title: Three extra fingerprint members added together
items.spec: Several single extra members each landed slightly below the incumbent but within noise (ErG 0.0884, Gobbi pharmacophore 0.0880, Avalon counts 0.0885). Add all three at once so their independent gains can accumulate. Extend fingerprints() to return six matrices: the current Morgan bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS, plus (a) rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(m), (b) the Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint folded to 2048 bits via Generate.Gen2DFingerprint with Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory and numpy conversion, and (c) pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP(m, nBits=1024) converted to a dense array. Fit the same XGBClassifier configuration on each of the six matrices, rankdata each class-1 probability and sum all six before the min-max scaling. Wrap each new featurizer in a try/except that falls back to a zero row for molecules that fail.

items.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour member
items.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member that is a similarity-weighted nearest-neighbour classifier, which captures local structure the tree models smooth over. Build RDKit ExplicitBitVect Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test molecules and compute the full test-by-train Tanimoto similarity matrix with DataStructs.BulkTanimotoSimilarity. For each test molecule take its k=15 most similar training molecules and predict sum(s_j^3 * y_j) / sum(s_j^3) over those neighbours (add 1e-9 to the denominator). Rankdata this vector and add it to `total` alongside the three XGBoost rank vectors, then min-max scale as now. The similarity matrix for ~1300 by ~300 molecules is cheap, so runtime barely changes.

items.title: Multilayer perceptron member on pooled features
items.spec: Add a fourth rank-averaged member of a completely different model family: a neural network. Pool the three existing feature matrices into X = hstack(Morgan bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS), apply log1p to the atom-pair count block (or to all of X, which is harmless for 0/1 blocks), then fit sklearn's MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3, batch_size=64, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, n_iter_no_change=20, random_state=seed) inside a Pipeline with StandardScaler(with_mean=False). Average the class-1 probabilities over three seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) to tame initialisation noise, rankdata the average, and add it to `total` before the existing min-max scaling.

items.title: Bit-dropout augmentation of the training rows
items.spec: Regularise the three XGBoost members with input-level augmentation instead of changing hyperparameters. For each feature set, build an augmented training matrix by stacking the original rows plus two corrupted copies: in each copy, independently zero out each nonzero entry with probability 0.15 using a numpy default_rng seeded with seed, keeping the labels unchanged (so the training set is 3x larger). Fit the existing XGBClassifier configuration on the augmented matrix, but lower n_estimators to 400 to keep runtime in budget, and predict on the untouched test matrix. Rank-average the three members as now. This teaches each model not to rely on any single substructure bit, which should help on folds of unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Replicate the ExtraTrees fourth member
items.spec: Re-run the slot-24 configuration unchanged to get a second measurement of its 0.0866 result, which is currently one noise-sized step below the incumbent and never replicated. Keep the incumbent three-feature-set XGBoost rank-average ensemble exactly as it is, and add one more rank-averaged member: a single sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier with n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, fitted on the horizontal concatenation of the three existing feature matrices (Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS keys) built by fingerprints(). Convert its predict_proba[:, 1] with scipy.stats.rankdata and add it to the running total with the same unit weight as each XGBoost member, then min-max scale the total as the current code already does. No other change; the point of this slot is purely a replicate, so do not retune anything.

items.title: Replicate the random-subspace XGBoost ensemble
items.spec: Re-run the slot-27 configuration unchanged to get a second measurement of its 0.0873 result. Replace the three per-feature-set XGBoost fits with a random-subspace ensemble over the pooled feature matrix: concatenate the three feature blocks from fingerprints() (Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts, MACCS keys) into one matrix, then fit 24 XGBClassifier models, each on an independently drawn random subset of roughly one third of the pooled columns, drawn with a numpy Generator seeded from the seed argument plus the member index. Use the incumbent XGBoost hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, eval_metric='logloss'), set n_jobs so total threads stay at 8, rank-transform each member's test probabilities with rankdata, sum them, and min-max scale the sum. Watch the 10-minute budget: if 24 members is too slow, drop to 16 but keep everything else identical and say so.

items.title: ExtraTrees member plus random-subspace XGBoost together
items.spec: Combine the two best unreplicated single changes into one script, since they lower loss through different mechanisms (model family diversity versus feature decorrelation) and may add. Build the pooled feature matrix by concatenating the three blocks from fingerprints(). First, fit 16 XGBClassifier models with the incumbent hyperparameters (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2), each on an independent random one-third subset of the pooled columns drawn from a numpy Generator seeded by seed plus member index. Second, fit one ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed) on the full pooled matrix. Rank-transform every model's positive-class test probability with rankdata, give the 16 subspace members total weight 1.0 (so 1/16 each) and the ExtraTrees member weight 0.5, sum, and min-max scale. Keep threads at 8 in total and stay inside the 10-minute limit.

items.title: All-ExtraTrees ensemble over the three feature sets
items.spec: Test whether ExtraTrees is simply the better learner here rather than just a useful extra voice. Keep fingerprints() and the rank-averaging structure of fit_predict exactly as they are, but replace the XGBClassifier inside the loop over feature sets with an ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=800, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, bootstrap=False, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), so there are three ExtraTrees fits, one each on Morgan presence bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS keys. Rank-transform each member's predict_proba[:, 1] and min-max scale the sum, as now. This is a clean model-family swap inside the proven three-feature-set architecture; report the loss even if it is worse, because a clearly worse result tells us the earlier 0.0866 was noise rather than a real ExtraTrees advantage.

items.title: Seed-average the whole ensemble three times
items.spec: Reduce the run-to-run variance of the incumbent rather than change its structure. Wrap the existing body of fit_predict in a loop over three sub-seeds derived from the seed argument (for example seed, seed+1000, seed+2000). For each sub-seed, build the three XGBoost members exactly as now (same hyperparameters, random_state set to the sub-seed) and accumulate the rank-transformed test probabilities of all nine resulting fits into one running total, then min-max scale the total once at the end. Do not change the feature sets or hyperparameters. Keep n_jobs at 8 and check the runtime: the incumbent job is well under the limit, but nine XGBoost fits per fold must still finish inside 10 minutes for all 15 fits; if it does not, cut to two sub-seeds.

items.title: Weight the rank average by inner out-of-fold AUROC
items.spec: Replace the equal weights in the rank average with weights earned on held-out training data. Inside fit_predict, run a 4-fold stratified inner cross-validation on the training set (StratifiedKFold with shuffle=True and random_state=seed) and, for each of the three feature sets, collect out-of-fold predictions from the incumbent XGBoost configuration; compute each feature set's inner AUROC with sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score. Turn the three scores into weights with w = max(auc - 0.5, 0.0), normalised to sum to one. Then refit each member on the full training set as now, rank-transform its test probabilities, combine with those weights, and min-max scale. The inner CV costs 12 extra XGBoost fits per fold, so reduce n_estimators to 300 for the inner fits only and confirm the whole job stays inside 10 minutes.

items.title: Inner-holdout early stopping for the boosting round count
items.spec: Let the data choose how many boosting rounds each member needs instead of fixing 500. Inside fit_predict, split off a stratified 15% inner validation set from the training molecules (random_state=seed). For each of the three feature sets, fit an XGBClassifier with n_estimators=2000 and the incumbent remaining hyperparameters, passing early_stopping_rounds=50 and eval_metric='auc' with the inner validation set as eval_set; note that the installed XGBoost rejects callbacks in fit(), so pass early_stopping_rounds through the constructor if fit() rejects it too. Record the chosen best_iteration, then refit that member on the full training set with n_estimators set to the best iteration scaled up by 1/0.85 (rounded) and predict the test set. Rank-average the three refits and min-max scale as now.

items.title: Multilayer perceptron member on folded fingerprints
items.spec: Add a genuinely different function class to the ensemble, since every tree-based fourth member so far has landed in the noise. Keep the three XGBoost members and the rank-averaging structure unchanged, and add a fourth rank-averaged member: an sklearn MLPClassifier fitted on the concatenation of the Morgan presence bits and the MACCS keys, with the atom-pair counts log1p-transformed and appended, all columns standardised with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold only. Use hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3, batch_size=64, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, n_iter_no_change=15, max_iter=300, random_state=seed. To damp the high seed variance of small neural nets, fit three MLPs with random_state seed, seed+1 and seed+2 and average their probabilities before the rank transform; give the averaged MLP the same unit weight as each XGBoost member.

items.title: Transductive label spreading over a Tanimoto neighbour graph
items.spec: Exploit the test SMILES, which are available at predict time, through graph smoothing rather than pseudo-labels. Compute 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan presence fingerprints for train and test molecules together as a packed boolean matrix and form the Tanimoto similarity between every molecule and every training molecule using matrix products of the bit matrix (intersection over union). For each molecule keep only its 15 most similar training molecules, zeroing the rest, symmetrise the resulting sparse affinity, and run sklearn.semi_supervised.LabelSpreading(kernel='precomputed'-style handling or an explicit few iterations of F <- alpha * S_norm @ F + (1-alpha) * Y with alpha=0.8 and 30 iterations) over the combined train-plus-test graph with training labels clamped. Rank-transform the resulting test scores and add them as a fourth unit-weight member to the incumbent three-member rank average, then min-max scale.

items.title: Feature-level mixup augmentation before boosting
items.spec: Augment each member's training set with convex combinations of same-class molecules to smooth the decision surface over scaffold gaps. For each of the three feature sets inside fit_predict, generate extra rows equal to the number of training molecules: sample pairs of training molecules that share the same label (draw from a numpy Generator seeded by seed plus the feature-set index), draw a mixing weight lam from Beta(0.4, 0.4), and set the synthetic row to lam * x_i + (1 - lam) * x_j with the shared label kept exact, so no label mixing is needed. Stack the synthetic rows under the real rows and fit the incumbent XGBClassifier configuration on the combined matrix. Keep the three-member rank average, the min-max scaling and all hyperparameters unchanged, so the only difference is the doubled training matrix.
